page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Intel-based n2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled at 2 threads per core. The processor is an Intel Xeon running at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, supported by a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 KB L1d cache. This instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per core. There is no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the n2-highcpu-4 generally operates in the lower performance tiers. Both single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, as well as Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, place this instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with Passmark memory scores and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the bottom 10% category. Large-block uncached memory read and write speeds are constrained at 27.14 GB/sec and 22.64 GB/sec respectively. However, the instance demonstrates average performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and Geekbench text processing.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2-highcpu-4 offers a dedicated CPU allocation at a lower entry point than higher-memory configurations, but its constrained 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU presents a significant resource density tradeoff. It is unsuitable for memory-heavy databases, large-scale compilation, or complex LLM inference. Instead, this instance is aligned with lightweight, compute-bound tasks that do not require substantial memory footprints, such as basic text processing, single-threaded data decompression, or low-traffic web serving where memory demands are predictable and minimal.
